FORE WORD
0.1 This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards lnatitution on 15 Febru~ 1978, after the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had been approved ~y_ the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council and the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1963. .This was revised in 19'1S

mainly in respect of tolerance. ~~JicabJe to varioua concentrations of the product and requirements of inity. Subsequently two amendments

were iuued andthese have been included in this revision. The second revision also incorporates the modified requirements pertaining to description, packuing and cautionary notice. For estimation of active ingredient a referenc~ has been given to Appendix A ot: IS: 1832-1978. in which an additional teat method hal been .incorporated. 0.3 Malathion water diapenible powder concentrates' are largely used in the control of pests of agriculture, public health and veterinary importance. 0.4 Malathion water dispersible ~wder formulation is generally manufactured to contain 25 percent (""m ) malathion content. 0.5 In the preparation of this standard, due consideration haa been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the rules framed thereunder. However, thilstandard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 0.6 For the pur~se of decidiDg whether a particular requirement of this standard i. complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or 8nalyad, sball be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-196Qt. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same .. that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This Itandard prescribes the requirements alld the method. of sampling and test for malathion water' dispersible powder concentrates.

5. TESTS

5.1 Tests 'shall be carried out by the methods n! prescribed -ln col 4 and 5 of 'fahltt 1.
5.1.1 For estimation of malathion content, start with a sample conmining 0-15 � 0-05 g of malathion into a 250 ml beaker. Add 50 ml of cyclohexane 'and stir for 20 minutes using a magnetic stirrer. Filter under reduced pressure and wash the insoluble residue on the filter paper with three l O-ml portions of cyclohexane; retaining the filtrate and wasbinp. Transfer quantitatively to a lOO-ml volumetric flask. make up to the mark \\ ith cyclohexane, and mix. Proceed with 10 ml of the aliquot for dctcJ"minjn~ malathion content as prescribed in Appendix A of
